note: Curated UX-metric signals for the dashboard — the quantitative analogue of voice_of_user.json. Each entry pairs a Helio comparison with the meaningful directional read of its scores. The dashboard renders the signal beneath that comparison's chart, alongside a variant 'Frontrunner' line it ALWAYS computes deterministically from the scores. So this file is for the editorial read, not the math. Re-curate each cycle (see the /new-issue skill, 'Dashboard signals'). Match a comparison by its compare_id (exact) or a case-insensitive substring of its displayed title. Cite real scores; never invent certainty. When Helio names variants after raw asset ids, an entry matched by compare_id may also set `title` and `variant_labels` (keyed by the variant's report id) — verify each label against the variant's thumbnail before adding it. Sources: Helio UX-metric compare pages, July and October 2026 cycles.
source: Helio UX-metric compare pages · July & October 2026

signals.title: Platform Menu: Data Management vs Our Platform

variant_labels.01M4RFWV7PA773DTSZ9HTPCJRY: B · Our Platform, AI Data Ready first

signals.signal: “Data Management” leads Overall UX (70 vs 58 and 55 for the two “Our Platform” versions) on sentiment alone (91 vs 61 and 46) — task success is a near-tie (44 vs 40 and 46), so the name changes how people feel about the menu, not whether they can use it.
signals.recommendation: Pick the name on positioning, not usability; if it stays “Our Platform”, lead with EDC — and rewrite item descriptions in plain terms either way.

signals.title: Newsroom benchmark: Everpure vs Apple, Spotify, Microsoft, VAST
signals.signal: Everpure's newsroom draws the highest Intent of the five (63) but the lowest comprehension (68, against 79 for Apple and Spotify) and the lowest overall score (57) — the top of the page doesn't say who Everpure is or which story matters most.
signals.recommendation: Add one clear lead story, a line saying who Everpure is, and a visible topic row and search — then re-test against this baseline.

signals.title: Certified Refurbished: Cisco, HPE and IBM programs
signals.signal: All three competitor programs read clearly (comprehension 70–78) but drive little Intent (18–32) — buyers want price, performance and warranty compared with new before they act. On Everpure's own site, task success for finding the program is just 33.
signals.recommendation: Give the program its own named line in the Products menu and lead its page with what the warranty and support cover.

signals.signal: Across four EDC variants, the EDC Page direction leads (+8 avg), with Sentiment the biggest mover (+18) — the redesign direction is working, and the assessment framing is starting to land in the verbatims.
signals.recommendation: Advance the EDC Page direction; keep clarifying the assessment payoff — it's still the friction point users name.

signals.signal: The Evergreen Architecture V2 redesign came in flat against State 1 — no average lift, and first-impression reads still default to generic “AI-powered storage” rather than the intended architecture story.
signals.recommendation: A visual pass alone isn't moving comprehension — try a different lever (plain-language framing, a labeled flow) before iterating again.

signals.signal: The Book Filter Default layout decisively beats the prior Platform Guides version (+39 avg), led by a large jump in task success — a clear redesign win.
Both relabeled CTA variants scored worse than the baseline — task success fell sharply. The new labels hurt rather than helped.
signals.recommendation: Hold the baseline CTA labels — don't ship V1/V2; rethink the labeling hypothesis before re-testing.

signals.signal: Eight rounds of iteration climbed to a peak around V4b, then V5b and V6 lost ground — V4b is the high-water mark the later rounds didn't beat.
signals.recommendation: Benchmark against V4b; diagnose what changed in V5b/V6 before another round of iteration.

signals.signal: Single screen: people grasp it, but it isn't landing emotionally — sentiment trails comprehension. (The related live-stream page fixes shipped and drew strong viewership — see this issue's Accelerate finding.)
More AI emphasis reads slightly better — the 75/25 mix leads on comprehension and sentiment; gaps are small and sample size isn't captured here, so treat as directional.
signals.recommendation: Lean the homepage toward the higher-AI mix, but confirm with a sized test before committing.

signals.signal: Single screen: comprehension of the actual offer is uneven — some restate the value cleanly, others invert it (“AI into data”), and the corpspeak draws fire.
